item.text: The second post’s first day produced 16 clicks at $2.09 each, versus 12 clicks at $2.83 for the first post over the same period. That’s promising, but still a small sample; I’ll give the comparison another day before shifting budget.

The second post has maintained its lower cost per click: $2.01 versus $2.89 overall for the first. I’m shifting most of the remaining budget toward it for the weekend. This is a traffic-efficiency decision; only your entry counts can establish which traffic converts.

Through Friday, the campaign has spent $267.23 and generated 110 link clicks. I’ve raised Saturday’s daily allowance for the second post to use more of the remaining budget during the Final Four; the combined $550 lifetime cap still applies.
Through Saturday, spend is $368.28 with 157 link clicks. I’m pacing Sunday to preserve budget for championship Monday. The second post remains ahead on cost per click, at about $2.07 versus $2.88.
Championship day starts with $99.71 remaining and 205 link clicks so far. I’ve made the remaining budget available today, with delivery scheduled to end at midnight Chicago time.
The campaign has ended at midnight Chicago time and is paused. I’m allowing one more hour for reporting to update before pulling the recap.
